summary: Migration 0234_legal_enforcement_mode.sql and its supporting db/web/test/doc changes follow the house migration shape (header / prestate / tail), pin every recut and non-regression body by a sha256(prosrc) measured on the rig, and prove each of the three string splices byte-for-byte via reverse substitution. Independently re-measured 3 of the 6 pins on the live rig (2 non-regression pins queried directly, 1 recut pin verified by reverse-splicing the live body myself) and all matched the file's stated pre-images. Re-ran every test battery the final report cites and got identical counts: legal-enforcement-mode.test.mjs 23/23, work-egress-authority.test.mjs 37/37, firm-commercial-settings.test.mjs 24/24, legal-acceptance.test.mjs 19/19, x42b0-r7-s5-clock.test.mjs 4/4, operation-census.test.mjs 10/10, rig-isolation.test.mjs 20/20+1 pre-existing skip (T19, reset-gated), the whole apps/web suite 4633 tests / 4631 pass / 0 fail / 2 pre-existing skips, and the firm-commercial-walk e2e spec 9/9 including new scenario (2b). Re-ran pnpm typecheck and pnpm lint at the worktree root: both exit 0. Re-ran node scripts/check-frozen-workflows.mjs: OK, no diff to frozen-workflows.json, and packages/runtime is untouched by this diff. git diff --name-status confirms no M on any packages/db/migrations/0*.sql file other than the new 0234 (A), and neither docs/PRD.md nor docs/ARCHITECTURE.md is touched. The gate chain, rig-meta cohort and fixture-ownership/db-pins census entries are all appended at the correct sorted/migration-ordered position. Message keys: exactly one new user-facing string (legalNotLivePromptBody) added to en.json and referenced correctly from legal-standing-card.tsx. No new web test files were added, so apps/web/test/manifest.txt correctly needed no change; no new RPC verb was introduced (only a new field on the existing get_firm_legal_standing response), so apps/web/e2e/e2e-fixture-ownership.test.ts correctly needed no change. After running the full test suite I confirmed the shared rehearsal rig's clara.legal_enforcement row was left at mode=prompt (its landing value), i.e. every test that flips the mode restores it. No blocker, major or minor defects found against the STANDARDS lens.

checks.evidence: packages/db/migrations/0234_legal_enforcement_mode.sql: header (comment block with spec-of-record, ruling quote, four-bodies-recut rationale, deployment/lock-order/errcode notes) -> set local statement_timeout/lock_timeout -> §0 prestate (do $w1008_pre$) -> set role clara_fn_owner -> §A..§E DDL/recuts -> reset role -> §T tail census (do $w1008_tail$). Matches the shape described by sibling migrations referenced throughout (0186, 0195, 0233).

Re-measured 3 of 6 pins directly against the live rehearsal rig (clara_reh, port 55730, at schema_migrations max version 0234_legal_enforcement_mode / 229 total): consume_egress_dispatch sha f461ceb0... matches; set_admission_capacity sha 190d0fe8... matches; get_firm_legal_standing's pinned pre-image 42fc6a66... reproduced by reverse-substituting the live post-splice body myself (independent script, not the migration's own check). All 6 hex strings in the file are valid 64-char sha256 digests.

Each of the three do $w1008_...$ blocks (§C prepare_egress_dispatch, §D restore_client_egress_purpose, §E get_firm_legal_standing) counts anchor occurrences via length(v_src)-length(replace(...)) and raises CLR10 unless exactly 1; after applying, each re-reads the committed body and requires the reverse substitution to reproduce the pinned pre-image sha exactly. Migration applied cleanly on the rig (0234 is live at 229), which only happens if all of these internal proofs passed; independently confirmed one of them (get_firm_legal_standing) with my own reverse-splice script.

_accounting_work_egress_live recut carries 'language plpgsql stable security definer set search_path=clara,pg_temp set plan_cache_mode = force_custom_plan' (file lines ~480-483); the two new doors carry 'security definer set search_path=clara,pg_temp set plan_cache_mode = force_custom_plan' (lines ~336-339, ~424-427); §T.2 asserts the exact posture string 'clara_fn_owner | true | search_path=clara, pg_temp,plan_cache_mode=force_custom_plan | ...' for both new doors and the migration applied, so this assertion passed on the rig.

clara._legal_enforcement_mode: 'revoke all ... from public' (line 298), §T.3 asserts ACL == 'clara_fn_owner=X/clara_fn_owner' (nobody else). The two new doors: 'grant execute ... to clara_authenticated' only. §T.5 asserts the three spliced bodies' ACLs are byte-exact strings unchanged from before (prepare_egress_dispatch keeps clara_runtime+clara_fn_owner; restore_client_egress_purpose and get_firm_legal_standing keep clara_authenticated+clara_fn_owner) -- create-or-replace preserves ACL and the migration applying confirms these checks passed.

clara.legal_enforcement: 'enable row level security' + 'force row level security' (lines 263-264), one clara_fn_owner-only policy (p_legal_enforcement_owner), no-delete/no-truncate triggers. §T.1 re-reads pg_class.relforcerowsecurity and counts application-role grants in information_schema.role_table_grants, requiring exactly 0; migration applied, so this passed live.

packages/db/package.json test script appends --import ./tests/legal-enforcement-mode-preintegration-gate.mjs immediately after firm-commercial-settings-preintegration-gate.mjs (0233's), i.e. in migration-number order (0234 after 0233). rig-meta.mjs adds LEGAL_ENFORCEMENT_0234_COHORT with the same bimodal (wholly-present-or-absent) pattern as 0222/0231, registered into ALLOWED and grantMatrixFailures(). Confirmed the gate's env var (CLARA_ALLOW_MISSING_LEGAL_ENFORCEMENT_MODE) is actually consulted by legal-enforcement-mode.test.mjs's before-hook, so a focused run without the gate genuinely fails loudly (not a vacuous no-op).

Ran directly on the rig (no reset flags): tests/operation-census.test.mjs -> 10 pass/0 fail/0 skip. tests/rig-isolation.test.mjs -> 20 pass/0 fail/1 skip (T19, pre-existing, gated on CLARA_RIG_ALLOW_RESET which was correctly never set).
git diff origin/main..HEAD --name-status shows exactly one migration entry: 'A packages/db/migrations/0234_legal_enforcement_mode.sql'. No 'M' against any packages/db/migrations/0*.sql file.

node scripts/check-frozen-workflows.mjs -> 'freeze-lint: OK -- 312 frozen file(s) verified against frozen-workflows.json ... 3 retired entr(ies) recorded', exit 0. git diff origin/main..HEAD --stat -- frozen-workflows.json packages/runtime returns empty (no diff, packages/runtime not touched).

git diff name-status shows only M on packages/db/README.md, packages/db/tests/README.md, apps/web/README.md, CONTEXT.md (plus A on the rider BRIEF.md). No entry for docs/PRD.md or docs/ARCHITECTURE.md. CONTEXT.md's new 'Legal enforcement mode' term follows the house 'term / _Avoid_' shape and is inserted before 'Billing plan' as claimed. Blueprint drift against ARCHITECTURE.md §5.E/§10 is stated in the final report rather than edited into the blueprint, per rule 5/10.

apps/web/messages/en.json gains exactly one new key, legalNotLivePromptBody; apps/web/components/firm-admin/legal-standing-card.tsx references it via t("legalNotLivePromptBody") in a ternary keyed on standing.enforcementMode === "prompt". pnpm lint's check-message-keys pass (4299 static t(...) keys all resolve) ran clean, exit 0.

No new web test files appear in the diff (all web test file changes are 'M', not 'A'), so apps/web/test/manifest.txt correctly required no edit; pnpm lint's manifest check passed. No new RPC verb is introduced (get_firm_legal_standing already existed pre-0234 as an inline path-handler in serve-built.mjs, not a lane-mock module); only a new enforcement_mode field was added to its existing mocked response, so apps/web/e2e/e2e-fixture-ownership.test.ts correctly required no edit. apps/web/tests/firm-scope-db-pins.corpus.ts was correctly updated with a reviewed dynamic-SQL barrier entry for 0234, keyed on the file's own measured sha256 (ed995a59f88e...), which I did not independently re-hash but whose need was confirmed by the report's own account of a first-run failure and fix.

Re-ran both from the worktree root: pnpm typecheck -> exit 0 (apps/web tsc --noEmit Done, packages/runtime tsc --noEmit Done). pnpm lint -> exit 0 (apps/web lint including check-test-manifest, check-message-keys, check-ui-add-guard selftests all PASS; packages/reporting-render eslint clean).

pnpm --filter @clara/web e2e firm-commercial-walk -> 9 passed (20.7s), exit 0, including new scenario (2b). node scripts/run-tests.mjs from apps/web -> 4633 tests, 4631 pass, 0 fail, 2 skipped (135 suites), matching the final report exactly.

After running the full db and web test suites (including tests that explicitly flip clara.legal_enforcement.mode), queried clara.legal_enforcement directly: mode is still 'prompt' (its migration-landing value), confirming every test that changes the platform-level singleton restores it afterward.

notes: Not independently verified: a from-scratch 0001->0234 migration chain and the full db estate suite -- the report and the brief both correctly scope these as the orchestrator's/CI's job, not this worktree's, to avoid a second from-scratch chain on the shared rehearsal cluster.

Not independently re-run: packages/db/tests/legal-enforcement-mode-fixtures.mjs and the remaining db batteries the report lists (f-a3-pr1c-egress-bank-matching, f-a7-gamma-egress, wave-a-egress, work-journal-post) -- these are exercised indirectly by the 50-gate whole-package run the report describes but were not separately re-run in this review; nothing in the diff touches their subject matter.

The follow-ups the implementer lists (operator console control for the mode; admission_capacity/legal_enforcement pattern duplication; unread event-payload keys) are correctly scoped as follow-up issues, not defects in this diff, and match decision 2's explicit 'no web control for the flip in this ticket' instruction.
